reviews.text: It is a little scattergun in its approach, and the ontology may be a bit much for kids, but even they will relate to its message about appreciating life’s smaller pleasures, which this year feels like a good one.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: A hectic, but wonderful celebration of life, and a moving animated ode to New York City’s jazz scene.
reviews.author: Diana Tuova

reviews.text: The studio’s first feature to frontline black characters is a stunning work of animation, with an important message to kids and adults alike.
reviews.author: Gautam Sunder

reviews.text: There are speeches within this film that I will take away for the rest of my life, that is how impactful this film is.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: While it's true that some themes such as "the meaning of life" could be inaccessible to younger viewers, Soul is also understood and works on a more basic level. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Some luminous musical numbers, the protagonist's transformation, and the visualization of concepts such as lost souls, or “no-body” lift a movie that finds its driving force in the reiteration of ideas... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rolando Gallego

reviews.text: Probably one of the more overlooked Pixar gems released, and it deserves so much more celebration and appreciation.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: Soul feels like a midlife crisis movie that has adults questioning their lives and children distracted by the bright colors.
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: If anything, Soul is guilty of over-ambition. The wizardry and wit are there, but it lacks Pixar’s usual deftness in making complex themes sing for youngsters.
reviews.author: Whelan Barzey

reviews.text: A classic Pixar feature, with the trademark emotionally powerful third act; a heartwarming, sweet, tear-inducing score; and a relatable, profound, well-explored story about our own soul and the meaning of life.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: I wouldn’t consider Soul a unanimous success, but its potential is undeniable. The impact and possibility this movie projects for future films at Pixar is key.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: Is it among the very best Pixar has to offer? No. Did it make me think and feel deeply the way that a Pixar film often does? Absolutely.
reviews.author: Brett Doze

reviews.text: ...it should help convince them that even if it’s not something they are great at, all they have to have is passion for its pursuit and that will be more than enough to satisfy their soul’s enrichment.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: An existential comedy that delivers beyond generic religious, psychological, life goals and ideals... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Soul is a thoughtful animated family film with a tender nature, some sweet laughs, and an even kinder heart.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Soul may not match the top-tier titles in Pixar’s formidable filmography, but this emotive exploration of human existence is just as engrossing all the same.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: Pete Docter’s gratifyingly inventive Soul is anchored in a similar site of broken chances and eluding hope, making it one of the most defining films of this year.
reviews.author: Ishita Sengupta

reviews.text: “Soul” is a heartfelt story about second chances and finding real purpose in your life. It’s about obsessions, mortality, and finding the true qualities that make each of us tick.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: While there’s plenty of zany action, including talking animals and a body swap, Soul is one of Pixar’s quietest, most contemplative, and gentle films. And for anyone who has questioned why you’re here, this will pack an emotional punch.
reviews.author: Daniel Howat

reviews.text: The film teeters on that fine line between genius and curiosity, going in directions that are unexpected even for a studio like Pixar. The film is confirmation that Pixar are still a company that do things their way, and that can only be a good thing.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Beyond its sillier humorous notes and efficient, fast-paced explanations of complex worlds, Soul rewards contemplation.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Soul is not just another masterpiece in the Pixar collection, but it is also the studios most thought-provoking and one of their most innovative features theyve made.
reviews.author: Mat Brunet

reviews.text: The film looks exceptional, the music sounds amazing, yet even with all the technical bells and whistles, Soul never forgets the emotional core and experience of its characters. It's a film that tells a story at a sensory level.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: An impressive technical achievement. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: The truth is that the film is presented as entertainment, but not so naively. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Only half a good movie. When mucking around with unfunny body-swap nonsense, it falls flat. When pondering the deep passions that give us reasons to live, it excels.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: It's comedic, moving and the animation is pristine. [But] [i]t's like animation meets Get Out, meets Magical Negro.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: I wish the film focused on and channeled more of its energy into that relationship and Joe's own life rather than his bump-in with 22.
reviews.author: Kirsten Acuna

reviews.text: Soul [is] a wildly ambitious, sometimes brilliant, gorgeously animated (in every sense of the word) film, all while breaking one of Disney/Pixar's biggest glass ceilings: an animated film featuring a Black lead character.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: [Soul] opens as a metaphysical theme park and morphs into a slapstick body-swap comedy ... It's a quietly joyous send-off to a relentlessly bleak year.
reviews.author: Selina Lee

reviews.text: It's solid Pixar working their magic with a couple rough spots but nothing to truly sour the experience.
reviews.author: Brittany N. Williams

reviews.text: Soul cannot make its discrete parts work as a whole of something when it feels like it is stuck in its own "Great Before".
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: With a simple, yet life-altering moral, wrapped in the greatness that we now expect from Pixar, it's no surprise as to why Soul is achieving a momentous amount of awards, while simultaneously being a perfect family voyage.
reviews.author: Andrew Dex

reviews.text: An animated film that infects me when it tackles with sensitivity and grace a rather clever concept that celebrates the value of human life. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Even if the story hits too many familiar beats to completely succeed, the animation is absolutely stunning.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: The film beautifully illustrates the communion of life's spark and human purpose. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: The shape-shifting keeps Soul light on its feet and keeps your eyes wide open.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: An animated masterpiece about a soul's adventure that will get you thinking and talking about the life and the afterlife, your passions and purpose, and the spark that sets it all going.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The film's multilayered charms - a Pixar hallmark - seamlessly blend heart and humor in a package that parents will be able to enjoy alongside their kids.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Directors Pete Docter and Kemp Powers manage to land these [existential] ideas. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Ponce

reviews.text: A smart, tender and contemplative piece of stunning filmmaking all on its own terms.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: This may be Pixar's most 'adult' film, in terms of its themes, its mostly middle-aged characters, its sometimes experimental and -- yes -- jazzy animation (heaven is run by characters who are nothing but squiggly lines), and its soundtrack.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: With its fragmented narrative, it feels almost like a shorts collection jazz riff on the theme of existence and metaphysics, plus quite a few of the jokes feel extremely American-specific and won't translate well for international audiences.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Pixar does some serious soul-searching embarking on an existential adventure that'll go to infinity and the great beyond!
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Even with some wrong notes, Soul has enough going for it to give it a reasonably toe-tapping recommendation. Just don't expect it to come together like a great piece of jazz.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Soul's overall message in conjunction with the surrealness of the afterlife and vibrant New York atmosphere leaves you with things to contemplate and appreciate.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: What follows is an absolute delight. It will make any viewer cherish the life they have and want to live it more fully, every single day, ideally with lots of laughs along the way.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: 'Soul' has magic, music and meaning.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Soul has a perfectly good message. Still, once director Pete Docter and co-director Kemp Powers, who both wrote the script with Mike Jones, lead us through how things work, they fall back on convention.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: Soul is beautifully structured and animated. Pixar remains undefeated at putting me through the emotional wringer.
reviews.author: Brian Gill

reviews.text: It is the story, and the message within it, above anything else, that is Soul's best achievement.
reviews.author: Shauna Fox

reviews.text: It shortchanges itself at every turn by overextending itself.
reviews.author: Kambole Campbell

reviews.text: Preaching to a mismatched choir that deserves a sermon that's more thoughtful and allows for greater individual interpretation than what is offered. But the animation is terrific!
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: One of Pixar's strongest works. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Ruiz

reviews.text: It's got a bebopping spirit that's difficult to resist.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: [There are] small moments that exude credibility but... go hand in hand with others that don't. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Amador Pérez Andújar

reviews.text: ...it would be hard to argue against Soul being one of 2020's most comforting, pleasurable films...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Soul feels timeless in the way most Pixar films do, rooted in a stylistic place but boasting themes and ideas, and magical worlds, that stretch beyond the now.
reviews.author: Tony Black

reviews.text: Not since the Beat movement has "soul" been so easily sold to all (meaning white hipsters).
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Like life itself, Soul is a messy and chaotic affair; a big bang where the physical and metaphysical collide.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: There's a lot of deep concepts in Soul, some of it's too complex for kids, but there is a mix of laughter, sweet music, mind bending animated visuals, and a message to live for today, not tomorrow.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Soul has a high concept premise and some truly gorgeous depictions of the afterlife and spirituality.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: The meat of the film is thoughtful, inventive, enlightening, but still quite heavy ... Foxx and Fey are a fearsome duo behind the voices, providing the right notes of humor and deep emotional resonance that will make you feel good by end credits.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: As per the Pixar mandate, there are laughs and plucked heartstrings, but Soul is after something deeper-an unusually curious examination of why we are the way we are...
reviews.author: Sean Fennessey

reviews.text: It would be doing a disservice to everyone involved with Soul to say what they've done is simple. Nearly everything about the film is memorable and thought-provoking, a rare thing no matter what type of story is being told.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Like the best Pixar films, Soul confronts a very ordinary existential crisis.
reviews.author: Brad Gullickson

reviews.text: Doctor, Powers and Mike Jones have written a sweet, simple, happy, sad, soul-stirring story that reminds you that every now and then that it's important to stop and smell the flowers.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Even with the film's bid for a suspension of racial disbelief, the racial-passing narrative in the second act of Soul is acutely bizarre.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Soul offers a soulful and sparkly treat of being alive and the joy of living..
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: The writing, music, and voice work made it all punch harder than the normal Pixar joint.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: Soul offers a surprisingly heady philosophical message to a distressed generation that is trying to find purpose through meaningful work.
reviews.author: Timothy Thomas

reviews.text: With a mixture of slapstick humor and gorgeous LSD-trip type images, the geniuses at Pixar pull it off.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: An entertaining, exuberant effort about our existence with comedic shenanigans, deep thoughts and wondrous imagination.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: It's funny, and it's imaginative, but it's also just very, very real.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: 'Soul' is another landmark film from Disney Pixar, likely to sweep next year's animated film awards.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: The movie is loaded with narrative and visual imagination. As is quite common in Pixar films, it may be just a cartoon, but it has plenty of soul.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The magic of Soul is how it marries the things we love in life with how we channel those things into goodwill for others.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Soul has multiple layers: kids will enjoy the animation of the characters, the physical comedy, and the music, while adults will be confronted with issues that, although are intrinsic to our existence, we tend to avoid. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Bond

reviews.text: Soul is a perfect movie.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Right when you think you get the message of the film, it turns another corner and you realize it's actually about something else. That makes this really good for rewatches.
reviews.author: Martin Thomas

reviews.text: Another example of Pixar's prodigious ability to elevate CG animation to a level of art that is astounding, thoughtful, emotive, and profound.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: It may not be your favorite Pixar, but there's no denying the imagination and lofty vision Pete Docter and Kemp Powers have with this film. And yes, like most Pixar, it very well may make you cry at the end.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: ...Easily Pixar's most adult film to date, and one that is likely to make you ponder and even question your own life choices.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: While it deals with grown-up topics such as the meaning of life, it tip-toes around the idea of mortality, choosing instead to put forward a candy-coloured cosmology that often suffocates its deeper questions under layers of whimsy.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: For a film like Soul it is more attractive to embellish and simplify the questions than to take a risk with their own answers.
reviews.author: Icnitl Y García

reviews.text: Soul is nuanced and layered, but it's not perfect. Yet, despite the serious themes, the richness of the narrative and the stunning jazz score make it more than worthwhile.
reviews.author: Aramide Tinubu

reviews.text: "Soul" may fail to fully follow through on its characters or its premise, but even a duller Pixar film will leave an impression.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: It's some of the most striking work that Pixar has ever turned in.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: Soul is about a person who happens to be black, and not a black American film. Have no confusion about that... But the film is really funny.
reviews.author: Charles Mudede

reviews.text: The meaning of "Soul" also comes through in the pointillist realism of Pixar. As delightful as its imagery of the afterlife is, the best stuff might be back on Earth.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: In the absence of transcendence, Terry tickled me into giggles. That'll do just fine.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: A little disappointment that, despite its formulaic essence, prevails as one of the best titles of 2020.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Indeed, it's frequently more complicated than it already sounds and yet it moves along so breezily... that its deeper resonances hit you in a way great art often does: unexpectedly and with a force that's sometimes difficult to explain.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: After plunging into the human mind in Inside Out and then the afterlife in Coco, Pixar Animation Studios takes us into both in Soul.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Soul is a beautiful film blending together the best-of-the-best of Pixar magic.
reviews.author: Lapacazo Magrira Sandoval

reviews.text: Amazing animation, serious themes in existential dramedy.
reviews.author: Sandie Angulo Chen

reviews.text: It's seriously fun. But the problem with explaining the massive questions of life via an eclectic hodgepodge of concepts gleaned from various spiritual and philosophical paths, is that only adults can shake this kind of thing off as mere entertainment.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: I'm not saying that Pixar is telling stories with the thematic complexity of an Ozu or Kubrick. I am saying that Pixar does what Disney does, only with more sophistication and layers.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Glad Pixar once again comes up with a fresh concept. A soulful film both thematically and in terms of the music genre. Pete Docter + team gives another imaginative insight into our humanity in the most delightful way.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: "Soul" has a lesson, one children can afford to learn, about our purpose in life, about our spark, about our music.
reviews.author: Martha K. Baker

reviews.text: The film is an ode to teachers.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: Delivering one of his finest performances in years, [Jamie Foxx] takes Docter and co-writer-director Kemp Powers'... excellent script and crafts an endearingly flawed character who feels like one of the most human Pixar have brought to life.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: It has a few things that just don't quite click for me, but I forgive them because it really is very emotionally touching.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: You can tell this is a movie where they put a lot of thought into what they wanted to take away from the message about souls and about what unites us... I think it is just an absolutely beautiful film.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: It's warm, it's charming, it's funny, [and] it has a terrific jazz score. It's a lovely film and has some very interesting, groundbreaking design work.
reviews.author: Charles Solomon

reviews.text: Delighting in possibility. It's heavenly screwball.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Docter does use his brightly colored, metaphysical version of It's a Wonderful Life to a good end. The movie doesn't just avoid the "pursue your dream at all costs" message we typically get from kids' entertainment. It positively rebukes it.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: Soul can remind us that being present with those we love, looking around at nature and the everyday turnings of our world is all we need to feel grateful for what we have, rather than focusing on that which we may have lost.
reviews.author: Jenny Desborough

reviews.text: Clever observations and funny lines deliciously intertwine in a eye-grabbing work of art that is both spiritually rich and terrestrially encouraging.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Its visual language is nuanced and lovely - particularly in character design - and its approach to the massive questions it poses is deft and moving.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Soul is another strong entry into Pixar's filmography, delivering a timely message during a pandemic. Its somewhat predictable story holds it back from my top tier of Pixar films, but with its strong message and memorable score, it's executed beautifully.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Sweet and sly, Soul is the hopeful note on which we needed to exit 2020. And it'll make a great way to start 2021 if you've yet to watch it.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Pixar, it's good to have you back.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: Although it is ostensibly about what lies before and after life, Soul is touching because, ultimately, it realizes that what really matters is what we do while it lasts. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: One of the best Pixar flicks in years, but still marred by positioning as yet another black animated movie where the protagonist spends a significant amount of the film's running time as something other than a black human being.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Pixar has made another animated classic with Soul.
reviews.author: Megan Williams

reviews.text: Soul marks a return to form for Pixar, tapping into the finite motifs and imaginative imagery that morphed the studio into a household staple.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: ...if a movie makes you want yourself and others to be their best self, how can anyone possibly be opposed to that?
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Expect a lot of questions because Soul throws out a lot of ideas, concepts and theories. The script ends up being like a jazz composition because of those elements.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: The film's score hums with jazz written and performed by Jonathan Batiste...Indeed, the film's most transcendent moments may well be those set not in the supernatural realm, but in a dark, crowded Manhattan jazz club.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text: Pixar's Soul is a tear-jerking animated adventure that taps into some weighty themes but proves incredibly touching for the whole family.
reviews.author: Lewis Knight

reviews.text: It isn't the cure-all balm for the soul you wish it was at the end of a terrible year. Its tacked-on ending might ring hollow for some. For others, it might just give them the hope to power through their crises.
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: With all its wonders and beauty, Soul is a significant step forward in representation, but also takes some steps back.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: Soul is yet another winning Pixar venture that hits you in all the right places with how it marries a whimsical animated adventure with humanity and meaning.
reviews.author: Suchin Mehrotra

reviews.text: [It] has its moments, but slammed together into one feature, they feel like they're fighting for dominance from one scene to the next, resulting in a film that, for all the work that's clearly gone into it, just doesn't seem to know what it wants to say.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: I love how strange Soul is, while still managing to feel at home in the Pixar universe.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: Both cleverly crafted (especially during the otherworldly sequences, with its Picasso-esque characters) and moving...
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: Music wallpapers every frame of Soul, with Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross sure to be nominated for another Oscar for their jazz-infused score.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: There's a lot to love. The animation is dope, and New York is captured in all its urban glory...it will have most adults in tears.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Not many will want to argue with the message and Pixar offers another deluge of creativity.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: A charming animated redemption story...
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It's rare that an animated feature from a big franchise leaves both adult and youth audiences pondering their purpose in life. Yet, Pixar and Disney's 'Soul' does this and so much more with humor, sensitivity and grace.
reviews.author: Lynnette Nicholas

reviews.text: "Soul" is a Disney+ feature that again demonstrates that animation can be a powerful way to tell a compelling story that would be difficult for live action.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Toggling between the two worlds, Soul finds a near extraordinary visual and sonic landscape.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: What this all adds up to is a gorgeous, very enjoyable and somewhat well-intentioned effort... Nevertheless, though it may aspire to the likes of Inside Out or Coco, Soul never quite reaches their heights.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: I feel like an ingrate as I complain about a mainstream Disney release that doesn't talk down to its audience, a Trojan horse of philosophizing packaged as shiny entertainment. But as much as I was intrigued by Soul, I didn't actually enjoy the experience
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Here's a film that's perfect for the entire family. Similar in tone to Disney's "Inside Out," kids and adults are shown that through our differences, we shine as people and that it's never too late to follow your dreams.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: If it's New Year joy you're after, then Soul should restore your sense of gratitude to overflowing.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: It's a giant leap forward for the Pixar folks: an intelligent meditation on what makes us, us, one predominantly geared at grown-ups.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: The pair's quest features race-against-time-adventure, bustling body-swap comedy and metaphysical flights of imagination.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: It's easy to become blase about the visual brilliance, both technical and artistic, of Pixar's output, but Soul really is a treat for the eyes.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: In its attempt to provide clever answers to unknowable questions, Soul just makes everything more confusing.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Soul adopts many of the elements and ideas that have made Pixar films so beloved over the years.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: "Soul" is all about who you are, what you wanted to be, fulfilling your life's dream. Don't see it stoned, or your mind will be blown. But it's not a lot of navel gazing or very preachy.
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: Spectacular music and visually astonishing. I felt it was beautiful that the film presents the idea that we're responsible for ourselves from even before our existence. A wake up call for many of us looking for answers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: Qualms aside, Soul is one of the more thought-provoking Pixar releases in years.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: The film, a lush, gorgeous work of animation that deserves to be seen on a large screen (my 65 inches don't cut it) proves to be intelligent, ambitious and reflective.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: This is one of Pixar's deepest and most melancholy animated comedies.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: It's a fiercely intelligent approach, funny and warm, knowing and insightful, and the way it expresses what's truly important is simply staggering.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Soul is certainly a movie that kids of all ages can enjoy for the visuals, loveable characters, and handful of slapstick laughs, but this is easiy Pixar's most mature film to date, as much, if not more, for adults than kids.
reviews.author: Caitlin Wyneken

reviews.text: Soul is the perfect escape to find yourself and while it may appeal more to adults than children, the animation will certainly capture the heart and soul, pun intended, of everyone who watches it.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: My favorite part was the earth-bound stuff, which featured one of the most evocative renderings of New York City I've ever seen on film, animated or not.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Soul looks astonishing throughout, a triumph of technical achievement, but it's not matched by clarity of story. It feels like there are too many cooks -- or to use the film's own metaphor, too many band members playing a different tune.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: "Soul" is a great time for younger viewers but for adults it touches on that sense of feeling the frustration of our big dreams. This is a rare animated film in how it tackles that subject.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: In a year in which more attention has been paid to Black death than ever before, Soul's adherence to yet another unnecessary Black out-of-body experience becomes even more tonally dissonant than it was before.
reviews.author: Monique Jones

reviews.text: The ambition of Docter's world building is laudable. And the smaller, human narrative he tries to tell within that universe is sweet and charming. But given its vast canvas, Soul sometimes struggles to focus on that more intimate story.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: It's funny, surprising, and powerful, but above all, it feels like Pixar returning to the core values that used to define it as a creative house, and returning to the inspiring industry leader it used to be.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: I can say that when it works, it's amazing stuff.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Soul is highly recommended -- especially to adults who might not be otherwise inclined -- and a return to form for Pixar after the less-satisfying Onward.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Soul is more abstract than past Pixar movies, but just as entertaining.
reviews.author: Rob Owen

reviews.text: [O]ne of the year's best films...smart and sharp and thought-provoking, all while offering plenty of lighthearted goofiness. It looks great, it sounds great ... it IS great. Soul shines - and sings.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: There were so many laugh out loud moments... it was it was just really delightful.
reviews.author: Achara Kirk

reviews.text: Having films like this for kids and adults is great because it helps us to sort of cope with those difficult concepts.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: Though the supporting cast and the score are worth the price of admission, Soul lands squarely in the middle of the pack when it comes to Pixar's legendary film canon.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: It's the final moments of Soul, however, that make it transcendent.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Not necessarily a bad film, per se, but it never quite manages to be as great, powerful or thought-provoking as it would clearly like to be.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: One thing Pixar films never fail to do is construct the "world" of their stories, and Soul has an ingenious attention to detail. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: Soul manages to speak to its broad demographics simultaneously, never letting weighty themes drag down its engaging narrative.
reviews.author: Ian Thomas Malone

reviews.text: A Pixar film that tackles mental health, depression and the meaning a life...seriously it does. Watch Soul!
reviews.author: Lauren Veneziani

reviews.text: It introduces several great concepts, themes and plots, but Soul doesn't give any of them the proper attention to grow.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Like a perfectly soothing, candlelit bath on an otherwise beastly cold night.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Soul is a bit more conventional in the end, but the approaches are recognizable and inspiring like in the best Pixar movies. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: A talented voice [cast]. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: It's another win for Pixar.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: There are stretches in Soul where Docter and his team are very much in the zone, crafting many magical and beguiling moments, only occasionally getting knocked out of it along the way.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: That directors Pete Docter and Kemp Powers have been able to tell a story about human nature, death and music through a family film is worth admiring. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Definitively not one of Pixar's all time greatest, but still colorful and spirited enough to take audiences into an enjoyable and heartfelt trip.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: I could not be more excited for families to get to see Soul! It's an emotional and heart-warming story that all levels will be able to appreciate in one way or another.
reviews.author: Dorian Parks

reviews.text: Soul is sneaky in a way that reminds you never to underestimate Pixar.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: The film recognizes the importance of jazz, and there's a welcome tribute to its history throughout this animated delight.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Magnificent animation proposal. A film set to become one of Pixar's classics. Thoughtful, intelligent and very funny. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diana Mangas

reviews.text: Soul meets Pixar's high standards of a visually compelling film that tackles heavy emotional issues in an entertaining way ... Just don't expect ... major representation of African American culture in the way that Pixar's Coco celebrated Mexican culture.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: An emotional cinematic celebration on many levels. When the history of Pixar is told, this will be one of their greatest films ... an instant classic to watch over and over.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: The animation and voice cast are outstanding. It has my favorite score of the year. There's not a lot to criticize. Soul is worthy of the Pixar banner.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: In this abstract assortment, everyone from Archimedes to New York's infamous Pizza Rat earns a mention and, somehow, it remains exhilarating. Go figure.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Soul is ... for sure one of the best animated films of the year, but ... it lacks a certain whimsy to appeal to children.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: Regular, old living is where it's at.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Unbelievably nice and sweet, to such a degree that it begins to lose some definition.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: There are so many lessons to learn from SOUL including a solid appreciation for pizza. I adore SOUL, because it causes kids to ask hard questions in an age-appropriate way.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: A spiritual cousin (of sorts) to Inside Out, Soul is another example of Pixar at its best. It's ambitious and inspiring filmmaking about life [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: There's richness all around, as it makes the intangible tangible. An important year-end flick for 2020.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: Frustrating sentimentality keeps the astral weirdness from the sublime, but it's a swing in the right high-concept direction.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: "Soul" ... confirms director Pete Docter as perhaps the greatest surrealist filmmaker since the Japanese legend Hayao Miyazaki.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A lot of Pixar films provide adults a whimsical look at life they've already experienced. Soul suggests the future is still ahead for those willing to embrace it.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: It's upper-middle-tier Pixar.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: There's so much joy, love, inspiration, truth, and wisdom within Soul. It shines light on the meaning of life that can be interpreted in many ways which is why the film is so beautiful.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: Soul stuffs its playful optimism into a simple message and delivers it with colorful, endearing beauty.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Conceptually simple, it carries a profound complexity beneath the surface, depicting an existential crisis that becomes a life-affirming examination of ambition, regret, obsession, insecurity, fear, and joy.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Clearly the best animated film of 2020. (Full Content Review for Parents - Scary Scenes, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Like other great New York movies, it invites you to identify particular intersections and storefronts, to compare its imagined geography with the city of your own experience.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Ultimately, the message of Soul is what sticks out the most about it, as it's uniquely refreshing to see questions like these aimed toward children, while still leaving enough room for productive conversation and, fittingly, introspection.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: "Soul" is a return to Pixar's roots of storytelling above all, but it also leaves me a bit melancholy.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Amazingly animated, perfectly voice-cast, and managing to surprise without losing focus, the more one thinks about Soul, the better it becomes.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: 'Soul' is the warm chicken soup and philosophical hug that we need right now.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: The plot of this film is ridiculous.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: 'Soul' offers an adventure that seamlessly balances insight with understanding. It's bright, beautiful, and emotionally affecting.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: A great cascade of entertainment, full of captivating ideas and brilliantly conceived supernatural visuals...the images director Pete Docter & his crew have conjured of these celestial netherworlds are at once compelling, beautiful and delightful.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: The film, like Docter's previous ones, is a great accomplishment of imagination, filled with real ideas, inventive design, and grounded by an emotional core...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: This film may contain the heftiest life lesson in a Disney/Pixar film that targets adults more than children. Even though this doesn't rank among the best of the studios' work, this still meets Pixar's high standards for storytelling.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Like the best jazz players, from Miles Davis to Kris Davis, Docter uses a traditional framework to branch off into new and exciting directions, without losing sight of the main theme.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: Soul represents another milestone for Pixar as it successfully mixes beautiful animation, inspiring music, and strong voice acting to create a uniquely brilliant experience.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: It's a wonderful life for Joe Gardner and whose love for jazz is animated for posterity through the words of Kemp Power and music of Jon Baptiste, Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: The film juggles interesting ideas, dramatizing them with great verve and deep feeling.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Docter and Powers do a remarkable job of making things flow in the best Pixar vein. It's very funny, of course, but the most memorable moments are existential, when characters experience small revelations, begin to see what life is about.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: 'Soul' focuses on dealing with the struggles of life and rising to the occasion, even if it means subverting your own goal to help someone else reach his or hers.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: It is both raucous and Zen as it tells the story of a jazz musician who is not ready for the Great Beyond, thereby becoming a perfect koan, and possibly the best movie of the decade.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Another major achievement from Pixar, and obvious contender for best animated feature awards.
reviews.author: John Wirt

reviews.text: A movie bursting to the seams with wild concepts, twists, and turns, almost to the point of feeling overloaded with them.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: A metaphysical dramedy set against an often trippy, post-Sergeant Pepper vision of life before life and life after death, Soul is an imaginatively rendered mid-life crisis.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: There's a beautiful sentiment that delivers a reminder to live life the fullest now, before it's too late. It's a message that stings even harder in the era of pandemic lockdowns.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Soul is about the things that make life worth living.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: I'll be watching that one again and again.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: A moving think piece that will stick with you long after the credits roll.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: An instructive fable infused with Pixar's on-brand pop philosophy. (You just know it's going to take you to a place that's 'moving').
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A really good Pixar animated film but not as good as I expected. A little less tine with the "blobs" would have sufficed.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: It is the perfect film at the perfect time and for that, it can get no better.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: To anyone of a certain age who has ever wrestled with similar fears and disappointments, Soul is sure to resonate, even if parts of it don't work as well as others.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Making life seem beautiful no matter the challenge is part of what I got from Pixar's Soul. And after I wiped the tears and quietly contemplated the film's message, I felt a little better about the world in general.
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Pixar has brought us another gorgeously animated, poignant story that transcends what most animated features do.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: There are many elaborate lessons on life and how to live it in Soul, though its best may ironically be its simplest: Look. Listen. Learn. Enjoy.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: A gorgeously animated, lovingly performed examination of the human condition.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: "Soul" challenges us to consider its heartfelt themes. We're reminded that the process of self-discovery always provides a solid foundation for great story-telling.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: The heavenly 'Soul' hits all the right notes.
reviews.author: Roger Tennis

reviews.text: There are times when watching this animated masterpiece feels like being gently indoctrinated into a new religion, one whose creed radiates tranquility, warmth and joy.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Beautifully animated. Some truly galaxy-brain New York jokes. But the ending is thematically troublesome in a way that betrays Pete Docter's usual confidence in his ideas. It's the first time we've seen his concept and execution get a bit crossed up.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Soul finds the company doing the minor-chord uplift it does so well, even an inch short of top form.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: This movie felt a little more mature to me in terms of the concept and the way the animation was done... It was really cool to see Pixar take a chance on something like this.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: 'Soul' is one of Pixar's best movies, but it's also the first targeted more towards adults than children.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: A Pete Docter film is strong enough in its own right to be placed in the higher tier of recent Pixar efforts, and while it may stumble from time to time, there's no denying that its heart is in the right place.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: Soul is going to be living inside me for a long time.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: This is the movie of the year for me. amazing voice performances, animation, score. I loved this movie!
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: I kind of wished this movie came out earlier...because I think people could have gotten something out of this. Super powerful movie. They had a killer screenplay.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: Soul ends on the perfect note, its last moments overflowing in voluminous human insights so melodious I could happily hum its climactic tune for a lifetime and likely never grow tired of hearing it.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Soul is perhaps the best film to come from the world of Pixar as director/co-writer Pete Docter manages to best his earlier film, Inside Out.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: I'll be damned if I don't appreciate it for honouring pizza with the screen time and the respect that it deserves.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Play it again, "Soul."
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Soul is an inspirational, laugh out loud funny, and purely joyous piece of entertainment for all ages that spans beyond our existential plane. As an animated film, it's beautifully animated, even by Pixar's high standards.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: There's as much to laugh about here as there is to take in the implications and complexities of what the beforelife and afterlife seem to be.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Soul feels easily like one of the best Pixar movies in years...
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It's a minor flick, to be sure, but the band is tight tonight and there's some pleasure in that if you give yourself over to it. It doesn't have fire, I'd say, but it's got a spark.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: Kids might be lulled by its dulcet presentation, but despite its big ideas, "Soul" is ambitious but flawed, a high concept high beam act that is a little too wobbly for its own good.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: There's a lot of poignancy to Soul without being bogged down in sentimentality. It's a cure for any existential malaise 2020 may have burdened on us, a celebration of the mundane and the grand, all-consuming passions.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: A figuratively astral journey full of imaginative moments that make us laugh as well as reflect on our position in life and the universe itself[ Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Filled with the right amount of humour and heart, Soul makes one feel all warm and fuzzy on the inside.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: What makes life meaningful? We are human because we ask this question, and the answer in part is to make movies like this one, to explore what makes life worthwhile.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The film's post-modern evocation of the afterlife, set to a nearly transcendent score by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross and the wistful jazz stylings of Jon Batiste, is unlike anything Pixar has done before.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: Like the finest Pixar pictures, 'Soul' engages both the brain and the heart, and does so in a visually entrancing fashion.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: "Soul" is messy, maudlin, funny, ridiculous, and poignant. In other words, it has soul.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Passing the love of jazz on to a younger generation, cloaked in the sweetness of an animated movie, is a genius move.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Like an ethereal cousin to his triumphant "Inside Out," "Soul" is another playful exercise in metaphysical world building, a door-slamming farce staged between the portals of consciousness.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: The vocal talents of this cast are that of seasoned professionals and they all bring their unique styles to the characters they portray.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Be ready for hard swallows, brow rubs, and exasperating "well..." sentence starters that follow the life-and-death questions being played with freely.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: The sharpest Pixar screenplay in years, with a screwball vibe and consistently witty use of cutaway gags. So much of it works at such a high level. What keeps it from achieving greatness?
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: Soul feels like a defiant anomaly, an actual risk that demands to be taken seriously. It may not be perfect, but it suggests a creative future for Pixar that hopefully heralds more fascinating results.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: Soul aims to provide a feel-good balm on what it means to be alive and to cherish every moment. And there is indeed a sublime beauty, thoughtfulness and tenderness to Joe's journey towards self-fulfilment and all that jazz.
reviews.author: Jeanmarie Tan

reviews.text: Much like Docter's previous Pixar films, the magic of Soul is not its sophistication; it's that the movie tackles complicated, adult themes in a way a child can at least relate to, if not fully understand.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: SOUL is a good Pixar film about not letting your life pass you by. It gets a bit lost in the middle but figures itself out by the end. .
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: The film is one of Disney/Pixar's best efforts in years. It's full of sublime attributes that eclipse many life-actioners this year.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Pixar's latest is a jazz composition that finds purpose in the quiet moments.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: "Soul" is a frustrating combination of artistry, charm and a Pixar formula that is starting to feel tuckered out.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The beauty of "Soul" is that, just as animation is finding more being demanded of it, Pixar is answering that demand.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Soul combines the abstract and the irreverent. As such, it also makes some unusual choices, some of which may stray from its most salient potential.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: A far more meaningful film now given the climate of the world at hand, Soul is a deeply-felt, oft-hilarious, more experimental effort from Pixar that serves as a lovely ode to both life and death.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Soul is an emotional story exploring the meaning of life, taking you on a magical journey with its stunning visuals, beautiful message, and delightful cast.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: It's a remarkable story, perhaps geared more toward adults than children, that sends a perfect message of living our best lives each and every day.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: It's a profound lesson that the best parts of life are what happens when you're not really paying attention.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: There's a definite satisfaction to how expectation-defying the film is, with its hairpin twists and turns, though some of the surprises stem from the way that Soul can't entirely figure out how its two worlds mesh together thematically.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: It's probably fitting that, in a film that urges us to embrace the everyday miracles of life, I found myself preferring the real world of "Soul" over its fantastic one.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Pete Docter's joyous "Soul" is a return to top-tier Pixar that tackles tough subjects while transcending age barriers. The best animated film of 2020.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Soul begins at full throttle... with visual discoveries. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yago García

reviews.text: Soul will doubtless keep its audience occupied for 100 minutes over this locked-down Christmas, but whether it'll win repeat viewers is another question.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: A great soundtrack, plenty of heart, and a stunning depiction of a life built on music, make Soul a journey that is worth undertaking.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Far from teaching children to follow their dreams, the movie... advocates leaving the dreaming to the pros.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: A bold and ambitious film about the perspective of life that made me feel seen not only as a Black person but also as a New Yorker and most importantly a human being.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Pixar's signature mature approach to resonant storytelling and visual wizardry is consistently on display here, as is their dedication to pushing the boundaries of originality.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: What truly deepens the film is the unexpected pivotit takes away from the "follow-your-dreams" message of a thousand Hollywood features into the less charted territory that lies beyond.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Soul is yet another homerun not just for director Pete Docter, who is almost scary good at this point, but also one of Pixar's best.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Like the best Pixar films, "Soul" isn't just for kids. There are lessons here for all ages, some surprisingly complex.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Pure genius and an absolute masterwork. A true, transcendental and euphoric experience for the eyes, ears and... yes... soul. A deep dive into the human psyche in the most meaningful way possible. It's one of Pixar's best of ALL TIME.
reviews.author: Dave Lee

reviews.text: This is a film in two parts and while the earthbound, jazz fueled pieces soar, the Great Before is another in a series of candy-colored representation of those intangible things which make us human...
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Arrives at some numbingly complex - and maybe not entirely consistent - answers, but generates some fun, and genuine beauty, along the way.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: It is an astonishingly beautiful film, one that plays with abstract, cartoonish animation forms in its scenes set in the Great Beyond and Great Before while also providing some of the best photorealistic digital animation.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Pixar's first feature with a predominantly Black cast and a Black lead actor (the superb Jamie Foxx) contemplates the origins of jazz and the meaning of life and death. Don't fret the metaphysics, kids, It's the year's peak achievement in animation.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: If the climax feels like a bit of a cop-out and the story is too complicated for younger children, Soul packs a real emotional wallop and it's unbelievably easy to get lost in the sheer wonder of it all.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Soul Is a Nearly Perfect, Beautiful, and Heartwarming Film.
reviews.author: Constance Gibbs

reviews.text: Featuring an outstanding voice cast, Soul deals with challenging concepts, yet they are presented to us in such a beautifully simple way.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Soul is marvellous on many fronts.
reviews.author: Aparita Bhandari

reviews.text: [Soul is] pleasant and clever, with a generous heart, committed voice acting, and some of the kookiest images in Pixar history.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: The latest tour de force from Pixar, Soul is a bold, conceptual jaunt across the astral plane.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Despite some distraction and not quite enough music, Soul manages to tap into deep emotion as its characters explore the limits of mortality and what it means to be passionate about life.
reviews.author: Sonia Saraiya

reviews.text: Inspirational and moving enough that like the best Pixar movies, it will get you feeling quite teary but also happy to be alive.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: That it's willing to ask such big questions of its characters (and in turn, the audience), and upend the tried-and-tested narrative structure counts for a lot.
reviews.author: Akhil Arora

reviews.text: Soul is a visual delight that strengthens the importance of the little things. (...) The perfect catharsis for the year we've had. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jesus Agudo

reviews.text: The pitfalls of Soul are less reflective of the actual story than they are of the reality that 25 years into releasing feature films, Pixar has become - dare it be said - a mite formulaic.
reviews.author: Josh Spiegel

reviews.text: As high-minded and celestial as its aspirations are, Soul never quite reaches the heights -- storytelling or emotional -- of past Pixar films.
reviews.author: Jim Vejvoda

reviews.text: Looking at the film as a whole, it teeters between being good and great, with the great portions being of typical excellent Pixar quality and the good portions being surprisingly average.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Soul feels, in the end, like a worthwhile Pixar experiment.
reviews.author: Dan Kois

reviews.text: 'Soul' is a splashy riff and a meandering tune that's unmistakably original. It may go off notes once or twice, but you won't be able to stop yourself from enjoying it right through.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Not one of Pixar's crown jewels, but a strong animated adventure. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: It seems like it isn't quite sure of its own conclusion.. Despite those issues, Soul is diverting, funny and thought-provoking.
reviews.author: Cynthia Vinney

reviews.text: It's got everything, really - even life itself.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Offensively implies -- in this year of all years -- that those who don't survive near-death experiences pass away because of a lack of inspiration or determination.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: ...when compared to other animated films, Soul soars into a different ball park, playing a different sport altogether...it's quite an achievement.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Most of the script's ideas are recycled -- or rather, reincarnated -- from A Matter of Life and Death and All of Me, but Soul has its own visual elegance, and an appealing line in pet-based humour.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Soul pushes Pixar further into uncharted territory than ever before.
reviews.author: Brandon Katz

reviews.text: "Soul" amounts to more than technical wizardry and intelligent dialogue. Why artists keep pounding the pavement despite never finding commercial success is a meaty topic.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Endeavoring to explore something as thematic towering as the meaning of life, Soul is one of Pixar's weightiest efforts to date.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Some of us grow up believing we could succeed in anything, which might be one of childhood's most well-intentioned and harmful lies. Soul might be one of the first children's films that rejects that well-intentioned lie instead of perpetuating it.
reviews.author: Hannah Lodge

reviews.text: A music-filled celebration of life.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It doesn't coalesce quite as well as some other Pixar films, but Soul is still a stunning, highly imaginative and poignant piece that continues to prove Pixar is one of the boldest and most innovative animation studios out there.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Yes, it can be funny and clever, but it feels too complacent and self-aggrandizing for its own good, a little too full of itself, to truly soar above the clouds like its predecessors.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Docter's most ambitious effort yet.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: [Docter] takes a look deep inside and comes up with another intuitive, easy-to-embrace metaphor for - dare I say it - the meaning of life.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Soul isn't Pixar's finest or most resonant film, but its beautiful animation and soundtrack, paired with fun characters make for an enjoyable watch.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: What follows is a case of body swap shenanigans, cat and mouse chases, and introspectively heartfelt ruminations on what it means to be alive.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Soul offers humor, yes. But it also offers a heart-filled exploration of life, living, and our impact that sometimes we forget to realize.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Pixar achieves animation greatness once more with a beautifully uplifting and creative film. Soul will make your heart soar.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: ...an exercise in psychedelic existentialism that astonishingly increases in inventiveness as it goes along.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: One of Pixar's most beautiful, poignant films, Soul often heads to some weird places, but does so in a way that will stick with you and leave you with a lot to think about.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: Among the year's loveliest, most poignant and moving pieces of work animated or otherwise.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: It's a bold, ambitious, challenging film that will appeal more to adults than kids.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: It's hard not to want Soul to be all about music, not just as metaphor but as the very real engine that drives the film's characters forward.
reviews.author: Dan Rubins

reviews.text: Sadly, this latest fantasy is never quite as funny, heartfelt, or moving as the pictures that preceded it.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: It's overflowing, like a bright portal into a new reality, with gorgeous details. So what if they don't quite add up to a deeper whole?
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Pixar finally moves beyond emotional manipulation to deliver a sophisticated masterpiece. Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross's score does a lot of the heavy lifting. Brilliant.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Like the best Pixar efforts, Soul is emotionally complex and life-affirming. It's a major accomplishment not just in animation, but American filmmaking period
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The film's disparate parts cohere beautifully in a bold take on life fulfilment that culminates in a finale as sweetly, softly poignant as Pixar's best.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: There are moments of true Blakean mystery and wonder here, expressed with a crispness that feels like a lightbulb snapping on above your head.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Hits deep, hits hard, hits heavy - but not quite soul quenching.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: Soul touches on life and death, heavy subject matter for a family film, and it's an emotional adventure that will inspire many to stop and smell the roses.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: A film that will have viewers ready to embrace life & live every day to the fullest. A deep movie that feels like it's made for adults, but one that kids will still enjoy.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: How wonderful it feels, amidst such havoc and cruel unpredictability, to be allowed some precious minutes to reflect on the beauty that lies in simply living.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: " 'Soul' is a mesmerizing return to form for Pixar; a veritable smorgasbord for the senses, vividly recapturing the joys hidden in life's most banal moments."
reviews.author: Jack King

reviews.text: It's a deeply sweet, happy, gentle film.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Ultimately it can't sustain moments in the same way as the likes of Inside Out, but it's certainly worth investing time into; even a lesser Pixar film is among the greater animated efforts being made today.
reviews.author: Daryl MacDonald

reviews.text: It doesn't hit its target, but its target is the key to life, the universe, and all that jazz. You can't aim much higher than that.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: A wonderfully vibrant & poignant journey celebrating life & the human experience, Soul is perhaps the most richly animated film of the year.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: Co-directed and written by Pete Docter and Kemp Powers, this is nourishment for, well, the soul. If you're feeling kind of blue, help is on its way.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It's sad, funny and beautifully realised.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: It's a concrete return to the Pixar of old, full of grand ideas and original execution, and a statement of intent for Docter's steering of the Pixar ship away from endless sequels and back to inventive originals.
reviews.author: Joe Utichi

reviews.text: There is fun to be had, but what would have been one of Pixar's best films had it been released a decade earlier now feels like one of their more formulaic efforts.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Soul doesn't hit the high benchmark that Pete Docter set with his previous Pixar movies, but it's still a profound, inventive and hilarious look at what it means to be alive.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: It is hard to think of another film this year so rich in character or so powerful in its emotional weight. Pixar had the ambition to make something as life-affirming and inspiring as A Matter of Life and Death for children. And they succeeded.
reviews.author: Liam Macleod

reviews.text: A hugely inventive tale about living life to the full that never, ever feels saccharine.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Narratively, Soul ticks nearly all of Pixar's boxes and as a film it's engaging, although one can't help to shake off the feeling that something's missing.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: For everyone who's ever felt they weren't good enough, Soul suggests a move towards accepting that life isn't something you can figure out on the first try.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Visually glorious, frequently very funny and genuinely profound...
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: "Soul" is perhaps the most existentially ambitious film ever attempted by Disney and yet it pops with colorful visuals and gentle wisdom while the story clips along despite the dizzying height of the concept.
reviews.author: Jason Solomons

reviews.text: While not quite offering the emotional gut-punch it promises, its many ideas never completely cohering, Soul is nevertheless a gorgeous and tender existential trip. It's full of surprises.
reviews.author: Alex Godfrey

reviews.text: [N]ot only does Soul live up to Pixar's own impossibly high standards, but it represents the very best the studio has to offer: beauty, humour, heart, and a gut-punch of an existential crisis.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Like some of the best jazz compositions, it uses a traditional framework to veer off in many unexpected directions, so that even the inevitable end point feels just right.
reviews.author: Kaleem Aftab

reviews.text: It's a vintage mix of the company's intricate storytelling, complex emotional intelligence, technical prowess and cerebral whimsy on dexamethasone.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

synopsis: Joe is a middle-school band teacher whose life hasn't quite gone the way he expected. His true passion is jazz -- and he's good. But when he travels to another realm to help someone find their passion, he soon discovers what it means to have soul.
